title: Can Humans Use Monitor Alerts? Replicating the AI-Sabotage Detection UX Study

original_idea.body: Run a small within-subjects study where CS-student peers review code diffs with sometimes-subtle backdoors under three alert formats (none, binary flag, flag-plus-explanation), measuring detection rate and review time.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: How monitor alert design affects human catch-rate is a defensible HITL runtime-control chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Small within-subjects peer study across alert formats; manageable but human-subjects coordination adds effort.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused detection-rate/time across three alert conditions; small-N study is one dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: HITL UX neglected by labs, lab-independent, feasible user study.

low_compute.reasoning: Light inference for alerts; human study compute-free.

novelty.reasoning: Extends a June 2026 study; the alert-design variable may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Source study exists; the alert-design comparison may be open.
